eventMetadata.context_description: Miami Heat travel to face Charlotte Hornets in the Eastern Conference NBA Play-In Tournament at Spectrum Center, a winner-advances showdown where the victor earns a shot at the 7-8 matchup for the No. 7 seed. Hornets clinched the 9th spot at 44-38, edging Heat's 43-39 mark for 10th and home-court edge. Miami's latest injury report confirms Nikola Jovic (ankle) and Dru Smith (foot) out, Pelle Larsson questionable (leg contusion), but Tyler Herro (foot), Andrew Wiggins (toe), and Simone Fontecchio (ankle) available after late upgrades. Charlotte boasts cleaner health sheets, with minimal listings like PJ Hall sidelined long-term, underscoring recent depth advantages and end-of-season form shaping trader sentiment in this high-stakes elimination game.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices California Governor Gavin Newsom as the frontrunner at 27% implied probability for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, driven by his executive experience, massive fundraising network, and high-profile criticisms of Trump administration policies, setting him apart from former Vice President Kamala Harris (6%), whose 2024 general election loss has eroded support despite some polling leads. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (8%) draws progressive and youth enthusiasm via social media savvy, while Sens. Jon Ossoff (6%) and Gov. Josh Shapiro (4%) benefit from swing-state victories. Recent catalysts include a March 2026 California primary poll showing Newsom leading Harris by 14 points and his February book tour signaling national ambitions. Consolidation could hinge on 2026 midterm results, Q2 fundraising disclosures, and early national primary polling, amid a fragmented field lacking a clear incumbent.

eventMetadata.context_description: Keiko Fujimori leads Peru's first-round presidential election tallies at around 17% with over 80% of votes counted by the National Office of Electoral Processes (ONPE), securing her advancement to the June 7 runoff amid a fragmented field of 35 candidates. Roberto Sánchez Palomino of Juntos por el Perú has surged to second at 12.5%, narrowly ahead of Rafael López Aliaga at 11.6%, consistent with Ipsos quick counts at 95.7% sampling, though final second-place certification remains pending due to April 12-13 voting delays from ballot shortages. Trader consensus prices Fujimori as the overall winner favorite, driven by her organizational strength, right-wing consolidation on crime and corruption—top voter concerns amid instability—and historical runoff resilience against divided opposition.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus prices Robert F. Kennedy Jr. at 49% implied probability for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, driven by his high-profile HHS Secretary role advancing Make America Healthy Again priorities, recent swing-state campaign appearances with GOP lawmakers, and family endorsements signaling intent despite prior denials. The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's April 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for April 28-29, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their April meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

Resilient March nonfarm payrolls adding 178,000 jobs and unemployment steady at 4.3% reinforce a firm labor market, aligning with Fed projections for just one 25 basis point cut later in 2026 per the March dot plot. Recent minutes indicate some openness to hikes if inflation persists, but traders see insufficient catalysts for action pre-meeting. A surprise escalation in geopolitical tensions or hotter-than-expected April CPI data could challenge this positioning, though base case remains steady policy.
